We need some new blood so before April let us see some form from such people as Miller, Thresher, Linstead, Johnston, Stearman, and a return to the team by Hallowell, Davies and Baulch (not new blood but almost indispensable).

August some of the boys went down to Brighton. Leroy clocked 22.9 in the 220 yds and 49.4 in the 440 yards, Thresher 4:15.3 in the Senior mile, and Bicourt 4:29.6 in the Junior mile.
CENTRE RIGHT: Walker, Black, Sawyer, Thresher and North head the field at 2½ miles in the Club 7 miles 6hampionship for the "Blackstaffe" shield.

On paper we had high hopes of being second to Portsmouth AC but once again we were unable to field a truly representative team and the ten that did start were dogged by misfortune.Those that were unable to appear were Linstead (injury), Thresher (cold), Newell (work) and Roffey (flu).

Gerry North was after Mal Robinson's Championship record of 4:15:8, but with Thresher and Kerr competing in the South v Midlands v North match at Wolverhampton he had to run solo for the final two laps.
Much of the glamour was robbed from the event due to the unavoidable absence of the North brothers, Thresher & Dabbs who were competing at major meetings.
With the absence of our best three runners of the moment---Gerry North, Kerr and Thresher---it was very encouraging to see such excellent running from the first four finishers.
However, despite the absence of Thresher, (defending his London County mile title) and Black and Fairclough (on holiday) we still finished a respectable 4th.

Pat forfeited a place in the "Brighton" team by his unfortunate retirement, which was caused by a week of indifferent health but with Gerry North, Thresher and Sawyer to come in with the first nine, none of our first 12 could be reasonably displaced.

Despite being without Gerry North, Thresher and Kerr our team still shook Portsmouth to the core over this course of six long and six short stages run alternately.
Could we do it this season with the following scorers ? SURREY: Gerry North, Thresher, Fairclough, Steer, Dabbs, Black. MIDDLESEX: Hart, O'Hara, Kerr, Newell, Dear and Crookes.
(Photo by Ron Linstead)--The Southern field after half a mile. Ringed athletes (l.to r.)are, Black, O'Hara,Fairclough,Hart, Steer,Thresher.

Our first eight, Gerry North, Thresher, Fairclough, Geoff. North, O'Hara, Dabbs, Thorpe and Black were to be joined by Hugh Barrow for the "National" at Sheffield, leaving runners of the class of Steer, Reilly and Hart as reserves.
Our 4th place was our best effort since 1948 and with Thresher and Barrow still to come our chances of further improvement next year are very good.
With Gerry North, Thresher and Barrow not running (besides other possibles like Newell, Reilly, Dance and Kerr) this surely would have produced our fastest "Brighton" team.
The following week saw three of our Woking performers (Dance, Steer and Black) joined by Thresher, Bicourt and Fairclough to form a strong sextet against tough opposition in the Blackheath Relay.

Well, I believe it will be Belgrave if the following team is turned out;- LONG STAGES: Gerry North, Fairclough, Thresher, Barrow, Hart, Kerr,. SHORT STAGES: Geoff North, O'Hara, Williams, Bicourt, Dance, Major,.

With a host of others just getting into the stride of the track season (Thresher 13:40.4/3m, Williams 4:12.7/1m, Geoff North "This year I'll hit the top or do nothing at all", etc.) I think we can look forward to what could be a vintage year for Belgrave.

To field a team of 10 and NOT turn out Thresher, Whewell, Fairclough, O'Hara and Steer and still finish fourth behind Coventry, Tipton, and Derby was no mean achievement and answered well for our own relay two weeks later.
The team that eventually took part was but a shadow of our full strength with names such as Fairclough, Hart, O'Hara, Steer, Thresher and Whewell missing from the line up.

His time was 44 seconds slower than last year's when he was run much closer by brother Geoff and Thresher. These two, plus Hart and Fairclough, were missing this time so Whewell and O'Hara were favourites to gain the place medals.

I wonder what Thresher, Fairclough, Major, Bicourt, O'Hara, Hart, Dabbs, Steer etc. think of that. Agreed that the North brothers, Dance, Whewell, Williams, Kerr and others have played parts of varying degrees in our success but they joined us on moving to London because they had to change their club.

With Thresher also absent O'Hara was the favourite - just. Our President, Ted Stimpson, sent the 45 starters scurrying up Lauriston Road and as they swirled round the corner one caught brief glimpses of "flash"Dance, "T.K.", "I'm only doing 60 miles a week" Newell, "Carnaby" Steer, "Photos" Linstead…

Sec. closed with a word of praise for our internationals during the year, Middleton, Thresher, Bicourt, Geoff North, Boosey and Lerwill as well as the promising juniors without whom the club would have no future.

There are always ifs and buts of course but will the loss of Diprose, the absence of Smith, the increased business pressure on Thresher and the moving house to Rochester of Geoff North have any serious effect?.

It coincides with the running into form, just at the right time, of Kerr, Thresher, North, Major and Fairclough. With Bicourt and Hart already in fine fettle we could well be having a celebration dip in the Lido on September 12th.
